paraphrase: The Goddess says to Bhairava: you have revealed to me all mantras and the sixty-four tantras of the Mothers, the best — Mahāmāyā, Śambara, Yoginījālaśambara, Tattvaśambara, the eight Bhairava tantras, the eight Bahurūpas, the eight Yāmalas, Candrajñāna, Vāsuki, Mahāsammohana, Mahocchuṣma, Vātula, Vātulottara, Hṛdbheda, Tantrabheda, Guhyatantra, Kāmika, Kalāvāda, Kalāsāra, Kubjikāmata, Tantrottara, Vīṇākhya, Trotala, Trotalottara, Pañcāmṛta, Rūpabheda, Bhūtoḍḍāmara, Kulasāra, Kuloḍḍīśa, Kulacūḍāmaṇi, Sarvajñānottara, Mahākālīmata, Mahālakṣmīmata, Siddhayogeśvarīmata, Kurūpikāmata, Devarūpikāmata, Sarvavīramata, Vimalāmata, the Eastern, Western, Southern, Northern and Niruttara, Vaiśeṣika, Jñāna, Vīrāvali, Aruṇeśa, Mohinīśa and Viśuddheśvara — these and crores of other śāstras, all made of knowledge, have been told by you.
speaker: the Goddess
notes: Phase-B author read the passage in the local e-text (sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/ebhAratI-sampat/AgamaH/tantrashAstram/nityAShoDashikArNavaH.md (Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava with Bhāskararāya's Setubandha)); level stays 'skeleton' until Phase C/D. Bhāskararāya's Setubandha glosses the eight Bhairavas as Asitāṅga, Ruru, Caṇḍa, Krodha, Unmatta, Kapālin, Bhīṣaṇa, Saṃhāra (noting other lists), the Bahurūpas as the tantras of the seven Mothers and Śivadūtī, discusses how the count of 64 is reached (e.g. 'mahādeva' as a vocative), and takes the Vāmakeśvara itself as the independent 65th tantra of Saundaryalaharī 31 (Gaurīkānta: the Jñānārṇava). Contribution from U08; U23 owns the Vāmakeśvara.

paraphrase: Tripurā goes to the supreme Person, markless, without qualities, devoid of the form of kula; then, free in her own form, taking the Lord of the world to herself and pleased by that path, she, alone, sports by herself — unmanifest Tripurā come to manifestation.
speaker: Bhairava
notes: Known here through the Yoginīhṛdayadīpikā's quotation (on YH 2.69-72, citing NṢA 4.12-16); only the latter part was seen, so the paraphrase is partial.

paraphrase: Around Tripurasundarī, the sixteenth, are the fifteen Nityās, each with her mantra, form and rite, worshipped in the triangle of the cakra.
speaker: Bhairava

paraphrase: The tantra teaches how the Śrīcakra is drawn — the central point, the triangles, the eight- and sixteen-petalled lotuses and the square — and how it is worshipped enclosure by enclosure with its deities, placements (nyāsa) and ten mudrās.
speaker: Bhairava
notes: Chapter-level summary; exact paṭala not recorded.
